writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 168 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
While striving for the Chinese Dream, young people enjoy more opportunities to realize their self-worth. As the nation advances, doors that were once closed are swinging open for the younger generation. Specifically, the rapid growth of technology, education and entrepreneurship offers a broad stage on which youth can turn their talents into real contributions.
These opportunities become meaningful only when young people seize them actively. Take my cousin as an example: instead of chasing a comfortable office job, she founded a start-up that brings online courses to rural children. For instance, thousands of students now learn from teachers they could never have met, and she has found genuine value in her work. In this way, personal ambition and national progress reinforce each other.
In a word, the Chinese Dream is not a distant slogan but a living platform that lets every young person shine. As long as we combine individual effort with the tide of the times, we can both realize our self-worth and push the country forward.

lines.en: W: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats. Welcome!
lines.zh: W: 今天的特别嘉宾是布莱克威尔勋爵，他是我国最具经验、最杰出的职业外交官之一。欢迎您！

lines.en: M: It's my pleasure.
lines.zh: M: 我很荣幸。

lines.en: W: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service. However, before we talk about that, I'd like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia. What can you tell us?
lines.zh: W: 我们的听众一定会非常想了解外交部门的职业生涯。不过，在谈这个之前，我想问问您今天新闻中有关Winopia共和国的最新事态发展。您能告诉我们些什么吗？

lines.en: M: I'm afraid I don't know much beyond what we've all seen on the news. It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on. But my career work has mostly focused around the continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I've never been involved with Winopian relations. It's for this reason that I don't know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
lines.zh: M: 恐怕除了我们都在新闻中看到的内容之外，我也不太了解。看起来，Winopia政府似乎正经历某种合法性危机，目前已经临时成立了一个过渡政府，直到各方就国家元首人选达成一致。不过，我的职业生涯主要集中在欧洲和美洲大陆地区，因此从未参与过与Winopia有关的外交事务。正因为如此，关于这件事，除了我们都能在报纸上读到的内容之外，我一无所知。

lines.en: W: Oh, I see.
lines.zh: W: 哦，我明白了。

lines.en: M: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our expert envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation, and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
lines.zh: M: 不过请放心，我们驻那里的领事馆中的专家特使会密切关注事态发展，我预计我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。

lines.en: W: So how does one get a career in foreign relations?
lines.zh: W: 那么，一个人要怎样才能从事外交事务呢？

lines.en: M: There are many different paths one can take. All diplomats have their own story. But in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering followed by six years' service in the air force. Then I went to law school, and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic corps where I have been for 22 years.
lines.zh: M: 可以选择的道路有很多。每位外交官都有自己的经历。不过就我而言，我先取得了电气工程学位，随后在空军服役了六年。之后我进入法学院学习，取得国际法学位后加入了外交使团，到现在已经22年了。

lines.en: W: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
lines.zh: W: 您认为从事这份工作需要哪些关键技能？

lines.en: M: There are so many. Being a hard worker and a good student is important. You never stop learning. In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric. Whether it is defusing attention or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
lines.zh: M: 需要的技能很多。勤奋工作、成绩优秀都很重要。学习永无止境。此外，外交官在表达和修辞方面必须非常清晰、善于表达。无论是化解紧张局势还是落实政策，人际交往能力和沟通能力都至关重要。

lines.en: M: It's getting late and we're both displaying signs of weariness. I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning.
lines.zh: M：天不早了，而且我们俩都显出疲态了。我觉得我们今天就到这里，明天早上再见吧。

lines.en: W: Oh, come on, Jeff. We are so close! Don't you think we are almost done? Let's do two more hours, please.

lines.en: M: One hour, then I'm going home.
lines.zh: M：那就一小时，之后我就回家。

lines.en: W: OK, fine. I think we are making good progress, and that with a few more amendments, we will be all done.
lines.zh: W：好吧，行。我觉得我们进展不错，再修改几处就全部完成了。

lines.en: M: I'm sure looking forward to it. I'm so tired of this project. Don't get me wrong. It's a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company, but it's just been so long.
lines.zh: M：我真盼着那一刻。我已经厌倦这个项目了。别误会，这对我来说是一次很好的职业机会，对公司来说也是一个里程碑，但这项目实在拖得太久了。

lines.en: W: Yeah. Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough. Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck, we'll be done by next week.
lines.zh: W：是啊。连续两个月只处理同一份合同，确实有点难熬。不过，我觉得如果运气好，我们下周就能完成。

lines.en: M: Ha, you must be delusional.
lines.zh: M：哈，你一定是妄想了。

lines.en: W: You don't think so?
lines.zh: W：你不这么认为吗？

lines.en: M: No chance. Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework. Then we need to proofread the whole thing and make sure all selling points are watertight.
lines.zh: M：没可能。第4、5、8和9部分还得按照新的框架进行统一调整。然后我们还要通读全文，确保所有卖点都无懈可击。

lines.en: W: But that will all take no more than a couple of days.
lines.zh: W：但这些加起来最多也就需要几天。

lines.en: M: I wasn't finished. When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen?
lines.zh: M：我还没说完。等我们完成后把它提交上去，你觉得会发生什么？

lines.en: W: What?
lines.zh: W：什么？

lines.en: M: They'll argue about it for like a month. There's always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made. They might think they're being helpful, but in reality they're being obstructive and hampering progress.
lines.zh: M：他们会为这事争论大概一个月。总会有个别董事插手，要求进行修改。他们可能以为自己是在帮忙，但实际上他们是在阻挠，拖慢进度。

lines.en: W: Oh, Jeff, you're too preoccupied and cynical. It won't be anywhere as bad as that. You'll see, the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible, and the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support. Go on then, let's stop there and meet up again same time tomorrow.
lines.zh: W：哦，Jeff，你太忧心忡忡，也太愤世嫉俗了。事情不会糟到那个地步的。你等着看吧，整个管理层都希望这个项目尽快实施，董事会也几乎一致支持。那就这样吧，我们今天先到这里，明天同一时间再见。

lines.en: One thing I've learned in a quarter-century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes. When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe. One such circumstance always comes back to me. It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution. Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth. We reached the deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, "Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for. He used to say, 'When in doubt, assume positive intent.'" And just like that, we had a path forward. My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter; quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees' stories. We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further. We assumed the best about both of them and moved on. The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us. In fact, their problems didn't recur. Over the years, this general approach has proved useful. Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
lines.zh: 我在四分之一世纪的管理工作中学到的一点是，人类行为中存在大量灰色地带，对于员工之间的纠纷，未必总能找到明确的是非对错解决方案。当两个人对同一事件有不同说法时，很难知道该相信谁。有一种类似情况我始终记得。事情发生在多年前，而这场冲突本身容易被遗忘，以至于我如今甚至想不起争议究竟是关于什么的，但我清楚地记得最后是如何解决的。两位才华横溢的年轻高管，其中一位由我负责管理，对同一事件的叙述大相径庭，我们似乎很可能永远无法查明真相。我们陷入了僵局，另一位员工的经理说：“我曾经跟随一位出色的经理工作，从他那里学到了一件事。他过去常说：‘当你无法确定时，就假定对方的动机是善意的。’”就这样，我们找到了前进的方向。我和那位同事一致认为，我们也许永远无法查明事情的实际情况；很可能两位员工的说法中都包含部分事实。我们同意继续观察他们今后的行为和关系，但不再进一步介入。我们对他们两人都作最好的设想，然后继续向前。结果是，我们得以把这场冲突抛在身后。事实上，他们的问题再也没有发生。多年来，这种总体处理方式一直很有用。每当真相模糊不清时，假定对方的动机是善意的，并同意继续向前，可能是一项具有建设性的决定。

lines.en: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for. For others, it's just a daily occurrence. And that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining. In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking. The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings. When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it and 45% had mixed feelings. Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing. As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing. Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby. Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion. Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out. However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash. Take buying lunch on workdays for example. People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch. Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less. One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home. Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry. It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
lines.zh: 对一些美国人来说，外出就餐是一种经过计划并纳入预算的享受。对另一些人来说，这只是每天都会发生的事情。随着喜欢烹饪的美国人数量不断减少，第二类人正在成为多数。21世纪初，研究人员埃迪·尹开展了一项调查，以了解美国人对烹饪的态度。调查发现，15%的美国人喜欢烹饪，50%的人表示讨厌烹饪，35%的人表示感受复杂。15年后，尹再次进行同样的调查，只有10%的受访者表示喜欢烹饪，45%的人表示讨厌烹饪，另有45%的人感受复杂。尹认为，烹饪类似于缝纫。就在20世纪初，许多美国人还会自己缝制衣服。如今，绝大多数美国人购买衣服，仍然缝纫的只是极少数人，而且他们主要是把缝纫当作一种爱好。尹认为，家庭厨师的数量也会以类似的方式减少。目前，美国普通家庭每年在外出就餐上的花费超过3,000美元。然而，人们在便利性上节省下来的，却会在现金支出上付出代价。以工作日购买午餐为例，人们购买午餐时平均每顿要花10美元。与此同时，自己准备午餐的成本会更低。一项调查发现，人们自带在家准备的午餐时，平均每顿只花费6.30美元。美国人日益不愿意花时间待在厨房里，这对食品杂货行业意味着一系列挑战。这种趋势也很可能会对家庭财务造成不利影响。

lines.en: Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing — and of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner. Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons. But the number-one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
lines.zh: 每年，在全球航班上办理托运的超过25亿件行李中，有2600万件会丢失；而在这2600万件中，有100万件永远无法回到原主人的手中。恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，以及有人单纯忘记取走自己的某件行李，都是造成这种情况的部分原因。但行李最终丢失的首要原因是没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它属于谁。

lines.en: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing. If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights. If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection but the passengers might miss the flight. Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit. Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination-coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate. Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
lines.zh: 将行李从值机柜台转运到出发登机口，再转运到到达登机口，最后送至行李提取处，需要精确掌握时间。如果整个系统运行得太慢，行李就赶不上联程航班；如果运行得太快，行李可能赶上了联程航班，但乘客却可能误机。每座机场都有自己的方式来分配行李在转运过程中所需的时间。有些机场拥有先进的自动化系统，包括能够读取行李标签的扫描仪、无需停下就能装卸行李的目的地编码车辆，以及将行李分拣至相应登机口的分拣机。即便如此，所有这些技术也未必能防止你的行李标签在传送带上被撕掉，使你成为一件无名行李的主人。

lines.en: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared "mishandled" by the carrier. Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged. Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours. The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination. If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days. Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse, and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
lines.zh: 行李一旦丢失，乘客提交索赔后，承运方就会将其认定为“处置不当”。“处置不当”是指行李延误、丢失、被盗或受损。大多数延误的行李只比主人晚一个航班，能够在24小时内送达。其他行李则由航空公司员工检查，以寻找有关其所有者和目的地的线索。如果谜团得以解开，这些行李会在四五天内归还给主人。没有目的地编码或身份标签的行李会被运往一个中央仓库，并在接下来的90天内接受全面的行李追踪调查。

lines.en: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions. It takes about three months to go from "missing in action" to "irretrievably lost". Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
lines.zh: 航空公司会对处置不当的行李进行登记，许多航空公司还会使用数据库，将行李内容与所有者的描述进行匹配。从“失联”到“无法追回的遗失”，大约需要三个月。一旦被认定为无法追回，这些行李就会捐给慈善机构、被拍卖，或由一家将其出售给公众的公司买走。

lines.en: So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage. And make sure your name is on the bag, along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.
lines.zh: 所以，千万不要把任何真正有价值的东西放在托运行李中。同时要确保行李上写有你的姓名和电话号码，这样工作人员就能联系到你。

lines.en: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone. And you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself. In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity. There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful. It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions. And it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy. Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
lines.zh: 你可能曾和这样的人在一起：他或她在与你互动时却忽视你，只顾摆弄智能手机。你自己可能也有过这种行为。最近的一项调查显示，十名受访者中有九人表示，他们在最近一次社交活动中使用过智能手机。也有证据表明，这种行为会损害社交关系。它可能使人们对面对面的互动感到不那么满意，还可能引发怨恨和嫉妒情绪。如今，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨了这些影响产生的原因。

lines.en: The study included 128 mostly female student participants. The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation. The conversation couldn't be heard but could be detected through mouth movements. Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
lines.zh: 这项研究包括128名学生参与者，其中大多数为女性。参与者观看了一段三分钟的动画，动画中两个卡通人物进行互动并交谈。对话内容听不见，但可以通过嘴部动作辨别出来。参与者必须设想自己就是视频中距离观众较近的那个人物，然后对对话作出判断，并评价自己对交谈对象的感受。

lines.en: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participants' conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation. In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone. A third version involved the participants' partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone. If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
lines.zh: 在实验的一种情境中，参与者的交谈对象始终没有使用放在桌上的手机。另一种情境中，交谈对象很快被手机上的某件事吸引，剩下的时间一直与手机互动。第三种情境中，参与者的交谈对象在使用手机互动和不理会手机之间交替进行。如果你曾经历过类似情况，实验结果大概不会让你感到意外。

lines.en: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions. The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
lines.zh: 参与者对社交互动中的手机使用持负面看法。手机使用出现得越多，他们认为互动质量和关系质量就越差。

lines.en: The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion. They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria. The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation. Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem.
lines.zh: 研究人员认为，把注意力放在手机上而不是身边的人身上之所以会产生这种影响，是因为这种行为被视为一种社会排斥形式。他们断言，这种行为类似于人们别无选择、只能独自在学校食堂吃饭的情形。不同之处在于，这种排斥发生在双方共享同一场面对面接触并进行交谈的过程中。研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊都产生了不利影响。

lines.en: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion. The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience. This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
lines.zh: 这些负面影响与传统社会排斥形式所造成的影响相似。这些新发现十分重要，因为它们加深了我们对日常体验中一种微妙却普遍存在的现象的理解。即使我们努力与他人建立联系，这种常见行为也可能造成疏离感不断加剧的恶性循环。

lines.en: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons. Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business. Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find. After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited, and the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
lines.zh: 越来越多的人出于各种原因旅行。许多人是游客，但也有许多人因个人事务或公务外出。不论出于何种旅行原因，旅行者普遍抱怨的一点是，他们所住的住宿场所缺乏个性。商务旅行者连续五晚住在五家相似的酒店后，可能会难以记清每天发生了什么，甚至记不住去过哪些城镇；而游客则可能产生一种错误印象，认为所有城市都大同小异，至少在装潢、食物和服务方面是如此。

lines.en: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or Bed and Breakfast arrangements. B&Bs, I mean, Bed and Breakfast arrangements are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting. For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles. And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America. The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed. But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
lines.zh: 为了消除这种千篇一律、缺乏个性的感受，旅行者开始利用家庭式接待或提供住宿加早餐的安排。我所说的B&B，就是住宿加早餐安排，指的是私人住宅在十分个性化且友好的环境中提供住宿和早餐。几十年来，B&B一直是游览欧洲，尤其是英伦群岛的经典方式。事实上，这在美国也并不是什么新鲜事。这一传统可以追溯到殖民时期，那时旅店十分稀少，疲惫的旅行者不得不依靠陌生人的善意来获得一顿饭和一张床。不过，B&B作为理想住宿方式的复兴，是相当近期的现象。

lines.en: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business. The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington, D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B. On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you. Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family. You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved. The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
lines.zh: 如果经营B&B的想法引起了你的兴趣，那么在贸然投入这项业务之前，有几个因素需要考虑。首先要考虑的是你的房产，不仅包括建筑物本身，还包括其位置。如果你住在著名历史遗址附近，或住在纽约市、华盛顿特区等热门目的地，你的房子即使相当普通，也仍然可以很好地经营成B&B。另一方面，如果你的房屋在建筑风格上独具特色，或拥有方便旅行者使用的设施，例如私人入口、私人浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意走相当远的路来投宿。另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。你必须考虑家庭的每一位成员是否真的喜欢接待客人，是否愿意反复谈论当地的景点和活动，以及是否有时间和精力承担由此增加的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和记账工作。最后还要考虑财务因素。潜在的B&B经营者必须现实地看待收入机会。虽然B&B通常前期成本较低，但专家估计，经营者至少需要定期出租五间客房，才能靠B&B维持生计。

passages.en: By now, it is generally accepted that regular exercise comes with an assortment of health benefits for people who maintain the habit over time. But is it __(26)__ too late to start?
passages.zh: 如今，人们普遍认为，对于长期保持这一习惯的人来说，规律锻炼会带来诸多健康益处。但开始锻炼是否有可能为时已晚？

passages.en: New research looked at people who increased their exercise levels after their 40s beyond levels they had when they were younger and those individuals showed declines in their risk of early __(27)__ which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives. This was a __(28)__ of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise. Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, which were similar to the steady exercisers.
passages.zh: 一项新研究考察了这样一些人：他们在四十多岁以后提高了运动量，超过了年轻时的运动水平。结果显示，这些人的早逝风险下降幅度与那些一生都坚持锻炼的人相近。与不锻炼的人相比，他们的早逝风险下降了32%至35%。那些在中年开始锻炼的人，慢性疾病的发病率也有所下降，例如心脏病和癌症，其降幅与持续锻炼者相近。

passages.en: So why bother exercising consistently throughout your life? The authors of the study __(30)__ that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __(31)__ . These real health benefits include better __(32)__ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. The latter is __(33)__ important given the global obesity epidemic. In addition, experts assert that starting younger is better because, if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those __(34)__ later in life. It is ideal, then, for people to start exercising when they are children or __(35)__ , and it is good to maintain an active lifestyle at all times regardless of your age. However, this study does indicate that, if you have not been active, you can still benefit if you start becoming active in your 40s and 50s.
passages.zh: 那么，为什么要一生坚持锻炼呢？该研究的作者承认，有些人可能会将研究结果理解为可以推迟开始锻炼，但这样做是错误的。坚持保持活跃还能带来其他身心方面的益处，我们不应忽视。这些真正的健康益处包括更好的认知功能以及较低的体重增加风险。鉴于全球肥胖流行的现状，后者尤其重要。此外，专家认为越早开始越好，因为如果你年轻时就养成锻炼的习惯，那么日后更有可能保持这些习惯。因此，理想情况下，人们应在儿童或青少年时期开始锻炼，并且无论年龄多大，始终保持积极的生活方式。不过，这项研究确实表明，如果你此前并不活跃，那么在四十多岁或五十多岁开始变得活跃，仍然能够从中受益。

J) mortality名词
形容词 early 后接名词作 of 短语的宾语

risk of early mortality = 早死风险，是流行病学固定表述 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 描述"早死风险的下降"，early mortality（早死）是公共卫生研究的标准术语；第二段后文又提 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases 谈疾病发病率，整段就是"死亡风险 + 疾病风险"双线索。
A)adolescentsearly adolescents 与 risk of 不构成有意义搭配 adolescents 是"青少年"，与 risk of 搭配不出"早期青少年的风险"这种话题；且 adolescents 留给第 35 题 when they are children or __(35)__ 与 children 并列才贴。
G) drop名词
This was a __ of 32% to 35%，空是单数名词作表语
drop of 32% to 35% = "32% 到 35% 的下降" 上文 declines in their risk of early __(27)__ 用到 declines（下降）；本句 This was a __(28)__ of 32% to 35% 的 This 就指代那个 decline，drop 与 decline 同义对接"下降幅度"。
I)maneuvermaneuver 是"操纵/策略"，不与百分比搭 maneuver of 32% to 35% 在英语里讲不通——maneuver 不表示数量增减，纯属词性对、语义偏的干扰。
C) chronic形容词
名词 diseases 前缺一个定语形容词

such as heart disease and cancer 是 chronic diseases 的典型例证 原文 reductions in their incidence of __(29)__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer——心脏病与癌症都是医学上的典型"慢性病"（chronic diseases）。such as 后的例子直接锁死形容词的语义指向。

D)cognitivecognitive diseases 不与 heart disease/cancer 类配 cognitive 指"认知的"，cognitive diseases 通常指阿尔茨海默等认知障碍；与 such as 后举出的 heart disease and cancer 不属同一范畴。且 cognitive 留给第 32 题 better __(32)__ functioning 与 functioning 搭配是"认知功能"的固定表达。 O)vocalvocal diseases 搭配不成立 vocal 指"直言的/嗓音的"，与心脏病、癌症完全无关，纯属词性对、语义不搭的干扰。
E) concede动词
主语 The authors + __ + that 宾语从句

concede 承认"研究结论可能被误读"这一让步语气 上下文 The authors of the study __(30)__ that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program but this would be a mistake. 是研究作者主动承认"有人可能会误读"——这是不利于研究主张的让步，再用 but this would be a mistake 反驳。concede（承认不利事实）正是这种"先让步、后反驳"的标志性动词。
M)refuterefute 与 that 后内容方向相反 refute 是"反驳"——若作者反驳了"some might interpret"这件事，后面就不会再出现 but this would be a mistake（反驳的反驳），逻辑跑偏；且 refute 的宾语通常是论点本身，而非"某些人可能这样理解"这一描述性事实。
最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— refute 与 concede 都能接 that 从句，最易反向。考生若忽略后半句 but this would be a mistake 的反驳信号，就可能错选 refute；防坑做法是先把整句的 but…mistake 看完，确认"先让步后反驳"的链条，再回头锁定 concede。
F) disregard动词
should not + 动词原形

disregard the benefits = 忽视这些好处 There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __(31)__.——"还有其他身心益处是我们不应当 ___ 的"，逻辑要的是"忽视"；disregard the benefits 是惯用搭配，且与下文 These real health benefits include better cognitive functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. 顺承——正因为不应忽视，所以列举出来。

E)concedeconcede 是"承认"，与"不应"组合后逻辑反 concede the benefits = "承认好处"，should not concede 变成"不应承认"，与作者鼓励大家重视好处的态度相悖；且 concede 在本文已被第 30 题占用是动词中性候选，留给第 30 更贴。 M)refuterefute the benefits 搭配勉强、语义反 refute 是"反驳（观点/论断）"，宾语通常是 claim/argument/theory；refute the benefits（反驳益处）既不常见，逻辑上 should not refute 也偏向辩论场景，与本句"忽视"含义不合。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— concede 与 disregard 都是动词原形、且都接抽象宾语，最易混。other benefits…that we should not __(31)__ 中考生若没注意到下文紧接着列举具体益处（better cognitive functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight），就可能误填 concede（"不应承认"），从而把作者的态度搞反；防坑做法是把空填后整段读一遍——作者要肯定益处，对应的动词必为"忽视"类。
D) cognitive形容词
比较级 better 后接"形容词 + 名词"，空是定语形容词
cognitive functioning 是"认知功能"的固定搭配 better __(32)__ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight 列举运动的真实健康好处——"更好的认知功能"与"降低增重风险"并列；cognitive functioning 是医学/心理学常用术语，正合此处。
O)vocalvocal functioning 不构成健康层面表述 vocal 指"嗓音的、直言的"，与运动带来的整体健康收益毫无逻辑关联，留作干扰。
K) particularly副词
is + __ + 形容词，副词修饰形容词
given the global obesity epidemic 提供了"尤其"的现实背景 The latter is __(33)__ important given the global obesity epidemic.——"鉴于全球肥胖流行病"这个背景子句直接为前面提供"尤其重要"的理由；particularly 与背景子句一拍即合。
B)arbitrarilyarbitrarily important 语义矛盾 arbitrarily 指"任意地、武断地"，与 important 搭配会变成"武断地重要"，逻辑相悖；六级阅读里副词修饰形容词，意思要相互配合而非矛盾。
L) patterns名词
those + __ 是名词复数作宾语

those patterns 回指前句的 "make a habit of exercising" if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those __(34)__ later in life. 中 those 指代前面的 "运动这种习惯"，patterns（模式/习惯）正好对接 habit；keep up patterns（保持这些模式/习惯）也是日常搭配。
A) adolescents名词
or 并列 children 的另一个复数名词
adolescents 与 children 并列指"儿童或青少年" start exercising when they are children or __(35)__——专家建议越早开始越好，最自然的并列就是"儿童或青少年"；adolescents 在年龄段上紧邻 children，词义与并列结构都吻合。

longreading.title: 2025年12月·第1套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. Since last summer, that has meant 11 am until 7 pm shifts at Caliburger in Pasadena, California, as well as short assignments at Chick-N-Tots at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. These are long hours of repetitive work, where the boss demands absolute consistency. But you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact. For Flippy is a robot — a cloud-connected mechanical arm with 3D thermal scanners for eyes — that can flip burgers or fry 80 baskets of food an hour, monitor that food and even clean up afterwards.
passages.zh: 和大多数厨师一样，Flippy 不惧怕辛苦工作。自去年夏天以来，这意味着它要在加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳的 Caliburger 餐厅进行上午 11 点至晚上 7 点的轮班工作，还要在洛杉矶道奇体育场的 Chick-N-Tots 餐厅承担短期工作。这些工作时间很长，内容也很重复，而老板要求绝对的一致性。但事实上，你不会听到 Flippy 抱怨，也不会听到它说任何话。因为 Flippy 是一个机器人——一只以云端连接、以 3D 热成像扫描仪为眼睛的机械臂——它每小时可以翻烤汉堡，或炸制 80 篮食物，监控食物，甚至在事后进行清理。

passages.en: B) Flippy was created by Miso Robotics, part of the Cali Group, which is described by its CEO, John Miller, as: "A technology company that happens to sell cheeseburgers." Cali creates new machines that it road-tests in its Caliburger restaurants across the world, into which Flippy will be deployed this year. And Flippy is not alone. Also in California, Bear Robotics has developed a self-guiding robot, Penny, which has so far served 40,000 diners.
passages.zh: Flippy 由 Miso Robotics 创造，该公司隶属于 Cali Group。Cali Group 的首席执行官约翰·米勒将其描述为：“一家恰好销售芝士汉堡的科技公司。”Cali Group 在全球各地的 Caliburger 餐厅中对新机器进行实地测试，Flippy 今年也将被部署到这些餐厅中。而且 Flippy 并不孤单。同样在加利福尼亚州，Bear Robotics 开发了一款能够自行导航的机器人 Penny，迄今为止已经为 4 万名食客提供过服务。

passages.en: C) Ten years ago, robot-chefs and waiters were pure science fiction. Today, they are a reality, and at prices that make them a plausible investment. From May, Penny will be shipped on a subscription basis that offers "an immediate return", says Bear Robotics' chief operating officer, Juan Higueros. Flippy will cost a reported $60,000 to $100,000. Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight — where customers order at screens, pay electronically, and eat food cooked and delivered by robots — are now a possibility.
passages.zh: 十年前，机器人厨师和机器人服务员还纯粹属于科幻小说。如今，它们已经成为现实，而且价格也使其成为一种可行的投资。Bear Robotics 的首席运营官胡安·伊格罗萨斯说，从五月起，Penny 将以订阅方式提供，这种方式能够带来“即时回报”。据报道，Flippy 的价格为 6 万至 10 万美元。由机器人烹饪并送上食物、顾客在屏幕上点餐、电子支付，并且只需极少人工监督的全自动汉堡餐厅，如今已经成为一种可能。

passages.en: D) The technology exists; it just needs knitting together cost-effectively and in a way diners buy into. In an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable. After an eight-month test at Kang Nam Tofu House in California, Bear Robotics credited Penny with driving a 28% increase in sales. Meanwhile, in US trials, the self-ordering screens that McDonald's is currently installing at its 1,300 UK restaurants yielded a reported 30% rise in order values.
passages.zh: 技术已经存在；现在只需要以具有成本效益的方式将其整合起来，并让食客接受。在这个渴望削减劳动力成本、提高利润的行业中，进一步实现自动化似乎不可避免。Bear Robotics 在加利福尼亚州 Kang Nam Tofu House 进行为期八个月的测试后，认为 Penny 使销售额提高了 28%。与此同时，在美国进行的试验中，麦当劳目前正在其英国 1,300 家餐厅安装的自助点餐屏幕，据报道使订单金额提高了 30%。

passages.en: E) Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology, alongside its ability to reliably push so-called "upsells" (meal deals, extras, larger drinks) to customers. Soon when you log into a restaurant app, it will be able to use your data and purchasing history to recommend dishes to you — factoring in everything from the weather to, if you are ordering at a screen that can read your face, your mood.
passages.zh: 人们认为，个性化是这项技术吸引力的关键，同时它还能够可靠地向顾客推销所谓的“追加销售”（套餐、额外配料、更大杯饮料）。不久以后，当你登录餐厅应用程序时，它将能够利用你的数据和购买历史向你推荐菜品——考虑到从天气到你心情在内的一切因素，后者适用于你在能够读取面部信息的屏幕上点餐的情况。

passages.en: F) "Right now people compromise on choice. We're presented with a one-size-fits-all menu. Ultimately, technology can allow us to make personal choices. You love spicy food and chicken? Here's the dish people like you mostly order," says Tom Weaver, CEO at the hospitality tech company Flyt. He talks enthusiastically about the Helsinki pop-up Take-In, a full-service restaurant where diners ordered dishes in from various delivery services. "For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants."
passages.zh: “目前，人们会在选择上作出妥协。我们面对的是一份适合所有人的统一菜单。归根结底，技术能够让我们作出个性化选择。你喜欢辛辣食物和鸡肉？这就是像你这样的人最常点的菜，”餐饮科技公司 Flyt 的首席执行官汤姆·韦弗说。他兴致勃勃地谈到赫尔辛基的快闪餐厅 Take-In：食客可以在这家提供全方位服务的餐厅里，从各种外卖服务中点入菜品。“几百年来第一次，数字技术让我们能够创造出新形式的餐厅。”

passages.en: G) If high-street fast food is automation-ready, its impact on high-end restaurants is likely to be subtler and slower. "It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield. "Apart from the AI creativity gap, great cooking involves a subtle understanding of ingredients and delicate cooking that would be enormously challenging for robots. Placing fragile foods on plates would be incredibly slow."
passages.zh: 如果说街边快餐已经准备好实现自动化，那么自动化对高档餐厅的影响可能会更加微妙，也会来得更慢。“我们可能还要很长时间才能看到五星级机器人厨师，”谢菲尔德大学人工智能与机器人学教授诺埃尔·沙基说。“除了人工智能在创造力方面存在差距之外，优秀的烹饪还需要对食材有细微的理解以及精细的烹调，这对机器人来说将极具挑战性。把易碎的食物摆放到盘子里会非常缓慢。”

passages.en: H) Currently, robots have limited functionality. A human needs to load Penny with plates that diners lift off themselves. At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans. But Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come. Modelled on the movements of a MasterChef contest winner, Tim Anderson, its robotic arms are fixed over a stove and programmed to prepare dishes from raw ingredients. It is designed for domestic use, but a commercial version is planned that opens up the possibility of restaurant kitchens automating even highly technically challenging tasks.
passages.zh: 目前，机器人的功能仍然有限。需要由人来给 Penny 装盘，食客再自行取下盘子。在由机器人驱动的美国披萨配送公司 Zume，更困难的工作，例如在披萨上添加配料，仍然由人完成。但即将推出的 Moley 展示了未来可能达到的复杂程度。它以《MasterChef》比赛冠军蒂姆·安德森的动作作为模型，其机械臂固定在炉灶上方，并经过编程，能够用生食材烹制菜肴。它的设计用途是家庭使用，但目前已经规划了商业版本，这为餐厅厨房实现高度技术性挑战任务的自动化提供了可能。

passages.en: I) For now, the kitchen technology that QSR Automations supplies to Mitchells & Butlers' pubs or KFC is less glamorous. Rather than having a chef shouting out diners' orders, the QSR system automatically distributes those orders across screens. The kitchen screens then tell chefs when to start cooking each dish, so that your plate of fish, chips and peas comes together at the right time.
passages.zh: 目前，QSR Automations 为 Mitchells & Butlers 的酒吧或 KFC 提供的厨房技术并没有那么光鲜。QSR 系统不再让厨师大声喊出食客的订单，而是自动将这些订单分配到各个屏幕上。厨房屏幕随后会告诉厨师何时开始烹制每道菜，这样你的鱼、薯条和豌豆就能在恰当的时间一起端上来。

passages.en: J) The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. "Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine.
passages.zh: 餐饮业目前正遭受严重的熟练厨师短缺——技能机构 People 1st 认为，缺口达到 11,000 人。“旨在让流程更不容易出错的自动化系统，正试图弥补这一缺口，”《Restaurant》杂志编辑斯特凡·乔姆卡说。

passages.en: K) In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age. Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark. Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but "lower than expected" acceptance.
passages.zh: 在简化或改善顾客体验方面，在线餐厅预订是互联网时代轻松取得成功的应用。自动化的桌边点餐和支付被视为下一个里程碑。在此之前，像曼彻斯特酒吧老板安迪·史密斯这样的早期采用者，可能会经历逐渐增加但“低于预期”的接受度。史密斯在自己的 33 Oldham Street 场所使用 Ordoo 应用程序。

passages.en: L) Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines. The TGI Fridays drone(无人机) that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites. But, says Chomka, such technology could miss the mark if it only offers "solutions to problems that don't really exist". "Payments being automatic" could be useful, he adds. But, in an expensive restaurant, "how quick do you need dinner to be?"
passages.zh: 餐厅科技令人尴尬的失败经常登上头条。比如，TGI Fridays 的无人机曾弄伤《Brooklyn Daily》的摄影记者；美国汉堡连锁店 Shake Shack 不得不放弃建立完全无现金点餐场所的计划。但乔姆卡说，如果这类技术只提供“针对实际上并不存在的问题的解决方案”，就可能无法达到目的。他补充说，“自动完成支付”可能会有用。但在一家昂贵的餐厅里，“你究竟需要晚餐有多快？”

passages.en: M) That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs. "Unite is concerned that without safeguards, any benefits will bypass workers in low-paying jobs, such as waiters," says the union's London regional officer, Dave Turnbull. "We're urging Members of Parliament to ensure automation does not just benefit a wealthy few like previous industrial revolutions."
passages.zh: 人们对待客这门人类艺术的依恋，会让那些把自动化视为就业威胁的员工感到欣慰。“Unite 工会担心，如果没有保障措施，任何好处都将绕过低薪工作者，例如服务员，”该工会伦敦地区负责人戴夫·特恩布尔说。“我们正在敦促议会议员确保自动化不会像以往的工业革命那样，只让少数富人受益。”

passages.en: N) The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively. Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number. "Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house. Last year, we recruited 1,000 new managers," says McDonald's COO, Jason Clark. Caliburger has a programme to retrain staff as robot engineers or "chef techs".
passages.zh: 业内的原则是，自动化将使其能够更有效地重新配置员工。工作岗位会发生变化，即使数量不会立即减少。“自助点餐屏幕意味着对前厅工作人员的需求会增加。去年，我们招聘了 1,000 名新经理，”麦当劳首席运营官杰森·克拉克说。Caliburger 有一项计划，将员工重新培训为机器人工程师或“厨师技术员”。

passages.en: O) But ultimately the chance to reduce overheads(管理费用) by employing fewer people or at lower rates will be what attracts big brands to technology. Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery. Companies such as Domino and Just Eat have both experimented with robot and drone delivery, which is already legal in Reykjavik, Iceland. "Robot food deliveries are the future," says Noel Sharkey. "Small, 4 mph ground robots are safe and will work 24 hours a day."
passages.zh: 但归根结底，通过雇用更少的人或以更低的工资雇人来降低管理费用的机会，才会是吸引大型品牌采用技术的原因。在未来 10 年里，传统实体餐厅的工作岗位必然会减少，其中一个重要原因是自动化将推动其发展迅速的竞争对手：配送。Domino 和 Just Eat 等公司都曾试验过机器人和无人机配送，而在冰岛雷克雅未克，这种配送已经合法。“机器人送餐就是未来，”诺埃尔·沙基说。“时速 4 英里的小型地面机器人很安全，并且每天 24 小时都能工作。”

passages.en: P) Combined with machine learning of anticipated order volumes and the minute-by-minute cooking data generated by systems such as QSR, that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly. "Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in," predicts Just Eat's director of engineering, Daniel Richardson. "I'll be able to say 'Let's have pizza' to my family, my intelligent assistant will hear and 10 minutes later the food will be at my door." No one is putting an exact date on it yet. But in the dining room and on your doorstep, the robots are coming.
passages.zh: 结合对预期订单量的机器学习，以及 QSR 等系统每分钟生成的烹饪数据，那支机器人队伍就能几乎即时完成配送。Just Eat 工程总监丹尼尔·理查森预测：“餐厅会提前准备好食物，以应对即将到来的订单。我可以对家人说‘我们吃披萨吧’，我的智能助手会听到，10 分钟后食物就会送到家门口。”目前还没有人给出确切的时间表。但无论是在餐厅用餐区，还是在你的家门口，机器人都正在到来。

statements.en: It is now possible to fully automate a burger restaurant with little human supervision.
statements.zh: 现在可以在几乎无需人工监督的情况下实现汉堡餐厅的全自动化。

analysis.锚点: 全自动汉堡店＋几乎无人监管
analysis.定位: C 段 Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight — where customers order at screens, pay electronically, and eat food cooked and delivered by robots — are now a possibility. 几乎无需人工监管的全自动汉堡店——顾客在屏幕上点单、电子支付、吃由机器人烹饪和配送的食物——如今已成为可能。
analysis.改写: It is now possible to fully automate a burger restaurant↔Fully automated burger restaurants … are now a possibility 名词转形容词的句式重构 with little human supervision↔managed with minimal human oversight 近义词成对替换
analysis.辨邻: D 该段重心是 further automation seems inevitable 的因由，没有题干要的"burger restaurant＋无人监管"组合。 In an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable

statements.en: At a robot-powered US company, complicated tasks still have to be performed by humans.
statements.zh: 在一家由机器人驱动的美国公司,复杂的任务仍然必须由人类来完成。

analysis.锚点: 机器人公司里复杂活仍靠人
analysis.定位: H 段 At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans. 在机器人驱动的美国披萨配送公司 Zume，较难的工作（比如给披萨加配料）仍由人来完成。
analysis.改写: complicated tasks↔the more difficult jobs 同义词替换 still have to be performed by humans↔are still done by humans 近义动词替换＋被动保持
analysis.辨邻: N 该段是 more demand for people front-of-house，针对的是"前台需求"，与题干"难活仍靠人"不是一回事。 Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house

statements.en: More automation appears to be a certainty in industries eager to cut labor costs and raise profits.
statements.zh: 在急于削减人工成本和提高利润的行业中,更多的自动化似乎是必然趋势。

analysis.锚点: 削减人工成本、提高利润
analysis.定位: D 段 In an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable. 在一个急于削减人工成本、提高利润的行业里，进一步的自动化看来是不可避免的。
analysis.改写: industries eager to cut labor costs and raise profits↔an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits 整组近义词替换 More automation appears to be a certainty↔further automation seems inevitable 名词化＋近义替换
analysis.辨邻: O 该段重心是 jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants，未陈述题干要的"更多自动化成必然"。 the chance to reduce overheads … by employing fewer people or at lower rates

statements.en: There are often front-page reports of failures in technological innovation of the restaurant industry.
statements.zh: 餐饮业技术创新失败的报道经常登上头版。

analysis.锚点: 餐饮科技失败常上头版
analysis.定位: L 段 Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines. 餐饮科技领域令人尴尬的失败经常登上新闻头条。
analysis.改写: front-page reports of failures↔failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines 习语转名词短语 often↔frequently 频率副词同义

statements.en: Robot-chef Flippy does not fear laborious work, nor does it make any complaints.
statements.zh: 机器人厨师Flippy不惧怕繁重的工作,也不会发出任何抱怨。

analysis.锚点: Flippy 不惧重活也不抱怨
analysis.定位: A 段 Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. … But you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact. 和大多数厨师一样，Flippy 不惧辛苦的工作。……但事实上，你听不到 Flippy 抱怨，甚至听不到它说任何话。
analysis.改写: does not fear laborious work↔is not afraid of hard work 近义词成对替换 nor does it make any complaints↔you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything 动词名词化＋否定保持

statements.en: Digital technology makes it possible for businesses to innovate restaurant models.
statements.zh: 数字技术使企业能够创新餐厅模式。

analysis.锚点: 数字技术使餐厅模式创新
analysis.定位: F 段 "For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants." "几百年来第一次，数字技术正让我们能够创造出餐厅的新形态。"
analysis.改写: Digital technology makes it possible for businesses to↔digital is allowing us to 近义动词替换 innovate restaurant models↔create new versions of restaurants 同义概括
analysis.辨邻: E 该段是 recommend dishes to you，落点在推荐与 upsell，未陈述"创新餐厅模式"。 Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology K 该段是 Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark，未陈述题干的"创新餐厅模式"。 online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age

statements.en: Fondness for human warmth in catering to customers will give hope to employees who are afraid of losing jobs to robots.
statements.zh: 对在顾客服务中体现人情温暖的偏爱将给那些害怕被机器人抢走工作的员工带来希望。

analysis.锚点: 人情味给怕失业者希望
analysis.定位: M 段 That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs. 那种对人性化待客艺术的依恋，会让那些视自动化为饭碗威胁的员工感到宽慰。
analysis.改写: Fondness for human warmth in catering to customers↔attachment to the human art of hospitality 近义词替换 give hope to employees who are afraid of losing jobs to robots↔heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs 形容词转动词短语＋同义重述
analysis.辨邻: N 该段是 Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number，落点在岗位结构而非"人性化待客带来的宽慰"。 The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively

statements.en: There is an acute shortage of experienced chefs in the catering industry and automated cooking is expected to fill the gap.
statements.zh: 餐饮业存在经验丰富的厨师严重短缺的问题,自动化烹饪有望填补这一空白。

analysis.锚点: 厨师严重短缺＋自动化补缺
analysis.定位: J 段 The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. "Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine. 餐饮业目前正遭遇熟练厨师的严重短缺——据技能机构 People 1st 称缺口达 11000 人。《Restaurant》杂志编辑 Stefan Chomka 说："旨在让流程更傻瓜化的自动化系统正试图弥合这一缺口。"
analysis.改写: an acute shortage of experienced chefs↔a severe shortage of skilled chefs 成对近义词替换 automated cooking is expected to fill the gap↔Automation systems … are trying to bridge that gap 近义动词替换
analysis.辨邻: N 该段是 more demand for people front-of-house，与题干"短缺＋补缺"不是同一命题。 Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house

statements.en: Over the coming decade, many jobs in traditional restaurants will disappear due to robot delivery.
statements.zh: 在未来十年中,由于机器人配送,传统餐厅的许多工作岗位将会消失。

analysis.锚点: 十年内传统餐厅岗位因送餐消失
analysis.定位: O 段 Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery. 无可避免地，未来十年，传统砖砌实体餐厅里的岗位将会消失，尤其因为自动化会助推它们快速增长的对手——外卖配送。
analysis.改写: Over the coming decade, many jobs in traditional restaurants will disappear↔over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants 近义词替换 due to robot delivery↔automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery 因果还原
analysis.辨邻: P 该段是 that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly，落点在送达速度，无题干的"岗位消失"。 Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in N 该段是 Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number，与题干"will disappear"立场相反。 Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number

statements.en: According to an expert in AI and robotics, it may be quite some time before a master robot-chef appears.
statements.zh: 根据一位人工智能和机器人技术专家的说法,可能还需要相当长的时间才会出现大师级机器人厨师。

analysis.锚点: AI 专家称大师机器人厨师尚远
analysis.定位: G 段 "It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield. "我们要见到五星级机器人厨师，恐怕还得很久很久，"谢菲尔德大学的 AI 与机器人学教授 Noel Sharkey 说。
analysis.改写: an expert in AI and robotics↔professor of AI and robotics 上位词替换 quite some time before a master robot-chef appears↔a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef 近义词替换
analysis.辨邻: O 该段是 Robot food deliveries are the future，话题为配送，与题干"机器人厨师尚远"无关。 Robot food deliveries are the future H 该段是 offers an idea of the sophistication to come，与题干"还要很久"的判断方向不同。 Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come

reading1.title: 2025年12月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
passages.zh: 许多人把友谊视为一条安慰毯：在你哭泣时可以依靠的肩膀，以及一个值得信赖、可以倾诉心事的人。然而，更多时候，我们急于追求个人成功，在前进的路上失去了朋友，而这已经成为这一过程的一部分。

passages.en: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.
passages.zh: 伴随日常生活而来的混乱与永无止境的动荡，是追求稳定友谊的巨大障碍。作为学生，我们用这个借口来淡然接受那些我们曾经以为是亲爱的人的离去。

passages.en: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
passages.zh: 我们不应把生活看作一场赛跑，仿佛每个人都在各自的道路上奔向某种形式的成功；相反，我们必须重新学会珍视自己在这条道路上建立的联系。我们必须重新评估激进的个人自由所带来的伤害。

passages.en: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.
passages.zh: 激进的个人主义将个人的自由置于集体之上。例如，它认为全民医疗保健这一集体主义的体现威胁到了许多美国人的梦想。

passages.en: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
passages.zh: 我们中的许多人都成了个人主义文化的受害者。社会往往赞美个人成就，并基于这样一种假设对其表示肯定：获胜或取得成功，是因为比下一个人更加努力。

passages.en: As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success". I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
passages.zh: 作为一个社会，我们把“在通往成功的路上失去朋友”这一观念奉为圭臬。我记得高中时听人说过：“别担心失去友谊，只管专心学习并考上大学。从长远来看，真正重要的就只有这些。”这种看法并非我个人经历所独有。许多成功故事都在宣扬这一点，而它也根植于我们看待成长的方式之中。励志演讲者会鼓动听众坦然接受失去朋友这一不可避免的结局。花太多时间和朋友相处？那你就是在浪费本可以更好地用于成就自己的时间。把时间投入到人际关系中？不如把时间投入到工作中。

passages.en: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.
passages.zh: 这种持续不断的成功需求使我们无法看清伴随日常生活而来的变动风暴。人们期待我们取得看得见的成功、赢得奖项、获得更高的职位、取得更好的成绩。为了成功，我们失去了朋友，而这令人遗憾地已经被正常化了。

passages.en: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
passages.zh: 我们不能甘于接受友谊的失去，因为友谊是我们的锚。是的，去追求成功。挑战自己。突破极限。但与那些自称成功专家的人所说的相反，独自完成并不会让你更加成功，也不会让你比那些在他人帮助下取得成功的人更优秀。

passages.en: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.
passages.zh: 努力培养健康的人际关系，并在那种似乎没有时间留给任何其他人的忙碌日程中维持这些关系。尽管我们可能生活在一个重视独立追求成就的社会中，但在前进的路上有人支持你、爱你，远比任何最终结果都重要。

questions.stem: What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success?
questions.stem_zh: 当人们急于追求个人成功时,常常会发生什么?

options.text: They lack a shoulder to cry on.
options.zh: 他们缺少一个可以倾诉的肩膀。

options.text: They have no soul to confide in.
options.zh: 他们没有可以吐露心声的知己。

options.text: They cannot find reliable friends.
options.zh: 他们找不到可靠的朋友。

options.text: They ignore their ties with friends.
options.zh: 他们忽视了与朋友的联系。

questions.判型: What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success? 是 What 引导的事实性问句，问 "经常发生什么"，无 infer/imply/suggest 等推断信号。
questions.拆句: What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success? 主句 What often happens 是 wh- 主语疑问句；when 引导时间状语从句，be eager to do 意为 "急于做某事"。句意 "当人们急于追求个人成功时，常常会发生什么？" 结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P1 However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process. 然而，多数情况下，在我们急于追求个人成功的过程中，我们沿途失去了朋友，而这已经成为这一过程的一部分。

locate.en: However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
locate.zh: 然而，多数情况下，在我们急于追求个人成功的过程中，我们沿途失去了朋友，而这已经成为这一过程的一部分。

option_analysis.note: They lack a shoulder to cry on. 把 a shoulder to cry on 这一对友谊功能的比喻直接当作 "人们当下缺什么" 的结论，但原文这一句是描述 "许多人对友谊的看法"，不是 "人们追求个人成功时发生的结果"。
They have no soul to confide in. 与 A 同套路，把 a reliable soul to confide in 这一对友谊作用的描绘当作题干所问的 "结果"，但原文这是 "友谊在人们眼中的样子"，不是 "追求成功时发生的事"。
They cannot find reliable friends. 说 "找不到可靠朋友"，但原文 we lose friends 强调的是 "主动放弃/丢失现有朋友"，与 "找不到" 是两种不同动作；原文从未说过 "找不到"。
在四项中，只有 They ignore their ties with friends. 与预判 "失去/疏远朋友" 在主谓宾三层都吻合，故选 D。

pairs.orig: we lose friends along the way
pairs.opt: They ignore their ties with friends.

questions.stem: What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism?
questions.stem_zh: 作者建议人们在追求激进个人主义时做什么?

options.text: Reexamine its detrimental effects.
options.zh: 重新审视其有害影响。

options.text: Shrug off the loss of their loved ones.
options.zh: 对失去所爱之人不以为意。

options.text: Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved.
options.zh: 避免其中涉及的混乱和动荡。

options.text: Remove aggressive obstacles in the way.
options.zh: 清除道路上咄咄逼人的障碍。

questions.判型: What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism? 直接问作者建议做什么，是对文中作者表态句的事实性提问，不是推断。
questions.拆句: What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism? advise sb. to do sth. = 建议某人做某事；their pursuit of radical individualism 是 "his/her/their + 名词 + of" 的所属结构，等价于 "when they pursue radical individualism"。句意：作者建议人们在追求极端个人主义时做什么？
questions.定位: P3 We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom. 我们必须重新评估极端个人自由的危害。

locate.en: We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
locate.zh: 我们必须重新评估极端个人自由的危害。

option_analysis.note: 在四项中，只有 Reexamine its detrimental effects. 同时覆盖了 "再审视" 与 "危害" 两个语义成分，故选 A。

pairs.orig: reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom

option_analysis.note: Shrug off the loss of their loved ones. 是 we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones 里被作者批判的 "错误做法"，并非作者建议。
Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved. 把 The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life 这一对生活状态的描述当作作者建议，但原文只是把它列为 "我们丢友谊的借口"，作者既未说要避免也未说要拥抱。
Remove aggressive obstacles in the way. 把 an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships 的名词搭配换皮成 "清除前进路上的强劲障碍"，但作者要清除的不是抽象意义上的 "前进路上的障碍"——他要重新评估的是极端个人主义之害。

questions.stem: What is American society's assumption of personal achievement?
questions.stem_zh: 美国社会对个人成就的假设是什么?

options.text: It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended.
options.zh: 它应当得到适当的庆祝和高度的赞扬。

options.text: It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream.
options.zh: 它是实现个人梦想的可靠途径。

options.text: It revolves around an individualistic culture.
options.zh: 它围绕个人主义文化展开。

options.text: It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor.
options.zh: 它反映了一个人非凡的努力。

questions.判型: What is American society's assumption of personal achievement? 是 What is 引导的事实性问句，问 "美国社会对个人成就的预设是什么"，无推断信号词。
questions.拆句: What is American society's assumption of personal achievement? American society's assumption of personal achievement 是双层所属结构：assumption of personal achievement 等于 "对个人成就的预设"；前置 American society's 进一步说明这是 "美国社会的"。句意：美国社会对个人成就的预设是什么？
questions.定位: P5 Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person. 社会倾向于赞美个人成就，并基于一种预设来推崇它，这种预设是：获胜或成功是比别人更努力工作的结果。

locate.en: Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
locate.zh: 社会倾向于赞美个人成就，并基于一种预设来推崇它，这种预设是：获胜或成功是比别人更努力工作的结果。

option_analysis.note: It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended. 把 Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it 的 "社会的做法" 直接当成 "对个人成就的预设"，但题干问的是 the assumption 这个预设本身的内容，不是社会怎么做。
It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream. 说 "个人成就是实现梦想的可靠途径"，原文从未将个人成就与 "实现梦想" 直接挂钩；原文涉及 dream 只出现在 threatened the dream of many Americans 中，且是普及医保的对立面，与个人成就的预设无关。
It revolves around an individualistic culture. 把 Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture 的上位归类（属于个人主义文化）当作预设本身，但题干问的是 "对个人成就所持的预设"，不是 "个人成就属于哪种文化"。
四项中只有 It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor. 准确捕捉 "成功背后是个人非凡努力" 这一预设，故选 D。

pairs.orig: winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person
pairs.opt: It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor.

questions.stem: What is preached in many success stories?
questions.stem_zh: 许多成功故事中宣扬的是什么?

options.text: Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success.
options.zh: 重视通往成功道路上的学业收获。

options.text: Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends.
options.zh: 把时间投入工作而不是与朋友交往。

options.text: Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success.
options.zh: 在追求个人成功的过程中努力加强友谊。

options.text: Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college.
options.zh: 在学业表现上出类拔萃以进入名牌大学。

questions.判型: What is preached in many success stories? 问的是 "很多励志故事中宣扬了什么"，是对文中具体表述的事实性追问。
questions.拆句: What is preached in many success stories? 主语 What 是宾语提前的 wh-；is preached 为被动语态，意为 "被宣扬"。句意：很多励志故事中宣扬的是什么？句式简单、无陷阱。
questions.定位: P6 Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead. 励志演讲者会推动听众坦然接受 "失去朋友" 这一不可避免的结局。和朋友花太多时间？你正在浪费本可用于个人成就的时间。把时间投入到人际关系上？不如把时间投入到工作上。

locate.en: Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
locate.zh: 励志演讲者会推动听众坦然接受 "失去朋友" 这一不可避免的结局。和朋友花太多时间？你正在浪费本可用于个人成就的时间。把时间投入到人际关系上？不如把时间投入到工作上。

option_analysis.note: Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success. 来自 Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college，但这是 "高中时听到的话"（作者的个人经历），紧接其后才提到 "a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories"——题干问的是 "在 many success stories 中被宣扬的"，即作者随后展开的演讲家观点，不是高中老师的话。
四项中只有 Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends. 同时覆盖 "投入工作" 与 "放弃朋友联系" 两层，故选 B。

pairs.orig: Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
pairs.opt: Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends.

option_analysis.note: Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success. 是作者自己在 P8 P9 提出的反向建议，不是 success stories 所宣扬的内容；many success stories 宣扬的恰恰是放弃友谊。

Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college. 同样源自 focus on study and getting into college 这句高中老师的话，且把 college 升级为 prestigious college（名校）属于无中生有；不属于 many success stories 所宣扬的内容。

questions.stem: What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success?
questions.stem_zh: 从文章中我们可以推断出关于追求成功的什么?

options.text: No one can succeed without pushing limits.
options.zh: 没有人能不突破极限而取得成功。

options.text: No one can afford to neglect close friends.
options.zh: 没有人能够承受忽视亲密朋友的后果。

options.text: Collectivism is superior to individualism.
options.zh: 集体主义优于个人主义。

options.text: Success experts often lead people to ruin.
options.zh: 成功学专家常常把人们引向毁灭。

questions.判型: What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success? 中 infer 一词直接亮明题型属性。
questions.拆句: What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success? What 作 infer 的宾语；regarding = 关于，介词短语作后置定语限定 infer 的范围。句意：关于追求成功，我们可以从本文推断出什么？句式平铺直叙。
questions.定位: P8 We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others. 我们不能对失去友谊袖手旁观，因为朋友是我们的锚。是的，去追求成功，挑战自己，突破极限。但与所有自封的成功专家所言相反，独自一人完成它，并不会让你更成功，也并不比那些借助他人之力成功的人更高一筹。

locate.en: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
locate.zh: 我们不能对失去友谊袖手旁观，因为朋友是我们的锚。是的，去追求成功，挑战自己，突破极限。但与所有自封的成功专家所言相反，独自一人完成它，并不会让你更成功，也并不比那些借助他人之力成功的人更高一筹。

option_analysis.note: No one can succeed without pushing limits. 借 Push limits 一词夸大为 "没有人不突破极限就能成功"，但原文仅说 "是的，去突破极限" 作为肯定后退一步的让步话，并未声明 "不突破极限就不能成功"。
在四项中，只有 No one can afford to neglect close friends. 是从 P8 P9 两处强表态合理延伸一步得到的结论，故选 B。

pairs.orig: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors.
pairs.opt: No one can afford to neglect close friends.

pairs.orig: having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result
pairs.opt: No one can afford to neglect close friends.

option_analysis.note: Collectivism is superior to individualism. 把 Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective 与 universal healthcare, an example of collectivism 加工成 "集体主义比个人主义优越" 的全称比较，但原文只反对 "极端" 个人主义，并未抬高集体主义本身。
Success experts often lead people to ruin. 来自 contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts，作者只是 "与所谓的成功专家相反"，并未宣称 "成功专家把人引向毁灭"——ruin 一词是文外强化。

reading2.title: 2025年12月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality."
passages.zh: 马丁·路德·金在诺贝尔和平奖获奖演说中说：“我相信，手无寸铁的真理和无条件的爱终将在现实中占据主导地位。”

passages.en: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.
passages.zh: 五十多年过去了，我们的社会仍在努力将真相与幻想、事实与虚构区分开来。从围绕气候变化的争议，到关于如何教授奴隶制历史的辩论，美国正处在十字路口。而争取公平是这些重要对话的核心。

passages.en: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
passages.zh: 一项又一项研究表明，不平等已经造成了骇人的后果。花旗集团在2020年的一份报告中指出，如果过去二十年间与高等教育相关的公平问题得到充分解决，“黑人学生一生的收入可能会增加900亿至1130亿美元”。

passages.en: This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation. It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
passages.zh: 这一统计数字反映出一系列我们作为一个国家未能面对的问题。它还凸显了一个事实：我们错失了弥合分歧、跨越隔阂的宝贵机会。然而，通过继承金的遗志，我们可以让国家重新走上实现真正公平的道路。

passages.en: Students — and adults for that matter — simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events. It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.
passages.zh: 学生，以及成年人，也无法在不了解当初起因的情况下，真正理解我们今天所面临的冲突。这意味着我们有责任帮助他们建立美国历史与当今事件之间的联系。这也意味着要为他们提供所需的工具，使他们能够处理自己生活中的不平等与偏见。坚持这些原则，并致力于开展真实的对话，可以帮助每一名学生更好地认识我们已经走了多远，也更清楚地看见我们仍有待走过的道路。

passages.en: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.
passages.zh: 通过更加真实地分析对更多合格且多元化教育工作者的需求，我们可以改进全国各地学校的招聘、培训和留任策略。

passages.en: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.
passages.zh: 遗憾的是，我们根深蒂固的分歧正在延缓这些进步。最近的一项调查发现，77%的美国人认为这个国家“比以往任何时候都更加分裂”。但关于两极分化加剧的报告不应使我们选择彼此回避。相反，这些报告应促使我们正面解决共同面临的问题。

passages.en: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.
passages.zh: 正如一些人所说的那样，我们并不是生活在一个“后种族社会”中。涉及种族不平等时，我们根本无法继续把头埋在沙子里。除非我们诚实面对不宽容、偏见，以及这些社会痼疾如何影响我们彼此对待的方式，否则不公正将继续纠缠着我们。但我们的子孙后代值得拥有更好的未来。

passages.en: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."
passages.zh: 在这个马丁·路德·金纪念日以及今后的日子里，让我们承诺共同努力，打破现状。让我们继续建设一个更美好、更包容的国家；用马丁·路德·金的话说，建设“一个与自身和平相处、能够与自己的良知共存的社会”。

questions.stem: What does the author think about today's America?
questions.stem_zh: 作者对当今美国有何看法?

options.text: It is struggling to transform fiction into reality.
options.zh: 美国正努力将虚构变为现实。

options.text: It has been the focus of many vital conversations.
options.zh: 美国一直是许多重要对话的焦点。

options.text: It still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized.
options.zh: 美国在真正实现公平之前还有很长的路要走。

options.text: It has got to a point where people disagree on nearly every issue.
options.zh: 美国已经到了人们在几乎每个问题上都存在分歧的地步。

questions.判型: 题干 What does the author think about today's America? 问的是作者对一个明确对象的具体看法，不是问全文主旨、不含 infer/imply。
questions.拆句: 句子结构是 What does the author think about today's America?，主语 the author、谓语 think、介词宾语 today's America；无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P4 However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity. 然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。

locate.en: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
locate.zh: 然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。

option_analysis.note: struggling to transform fiction into reality 的字面义是「努力把虚构变成现实」，与 struggling to separate truth from fantasy（努力分清真相与幻象）方向相反——原文是要分开两者，不是把虚构变成现实。
It has been the focus of many vital conversations 把美国当成「对话的焦点」；但 the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations 里说的是「公平之战是这些对话的核心」，焦点是 equity，不是美国。
预判「离真正公平还远」与 still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized 一一对应，且呼应 still struggling——锁定 C。

pairs.orig: get our country back on the path toward true equity
pairs.opt: still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized

pairs.orig: our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy
pairs.opt: still has a long way to go

option_analysis.note: disagree on nearly every issue 把分歧泛化到「几乎每一个议题」；原文只举了 climate change 与 how slavery is taught 等具体议题，且作者关心的核心是 equity，没有「几乎每个议题都有分歧」的论断。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years?
questions.stem_zh: 从文章中我们了解到过去20年中黑人学生的什么情况?

options.text: They have been unfairly treated regarding higher education.
options.zh: 他们在高等教育方面受到了不公平的对待。

options.text: They have been battling hard to address equity issues.
options.zh: 他们一直在努力奋斗以解决公平问题。

options.text: They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars.
options.zh: 他们使自己的终身收入增加了数十亿美元。

options.text: They have come to see the consequences of racial discrimination.
options.zh: 他们已经认识到种族歧视的后果。

questions.判型: 题干 What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years? 问从文中「得知」什么，明确锁定群体加时间，是要求回原文复述事实。
questions.拆句: What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years? 是 What...about... 结构，about 后跟的 black students in the past 20 years 是定位对象；结构清晰，无陷阱。
questions.定位: P3 A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades. 花旗集团 2020 年的一份报告指出：如果过去二十年里高等教育中的公平问题得到了妥善处理，黑人学生本可以多挣 900 亿到 1130 亿美元的终身收入。

locate.en: A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
locate.zh: 花旗集团 2020 年的一份报告指出：如果过去二十年里高等教育中的公平问题得到了妥善处理，黑人学生本可以多挣 900 亿到 1130 亿美元的终身收入。

option_analysis.note: 预判「过去二十年高等教育对黑人学生不公」与 unfairly treated regarding higher education 一一对应——锁定 A。

pairs.orig: if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades
Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion

option_analysis.note: battling hard to address equity issues 把「被动遭遇不公」换成「主动奋力解决公平问题」；原文只说公平问题如果被妥善处理黑人学生本可多挣钱，并未说他们自己在奋斗解决。
They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars 用现在完成时陈述「已经多挣了」；原文是 could have increased 虚拟语气，含义是「本可以但实际没有」——选项把虚拟当作了现实。
come to see the consequences of racial discrimination 把话题偷换成「看清种族歧视的后果」；原文谈的是高等教育公平问题与黑人学生的收入损失，并未提及他们「认识到歧视后果」这一心理变化。

questions.stem: How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them?
questions.stem_zh: 美国人如何能够弥合分裂他们的分歧?

options.text: By dealing with the thorny issues confronting them.
options.zh: 通过处理他们面临的棘手问题。

options.text: By seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony.
options.zh: 通过抓住每个机会来增进种族和谐。

options.text: By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause.
options.zh: 通过继续追求Martin Luther King Jr.的事业。

options.text: By striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities.
options.zh: 通过努力识别极其宝贵的机会。

questions.判型: 题干 How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them? 问的是「如何做到 X」，要求从原文找具体路径，是细节题。
questions.拆句: How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them? 中 that divide them 是定语从句修饰 differences，等于 the differences which divide Americans；结构稍长，但无否定无比较，逻辑直白。
questions.定位: P4 However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity. 然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。

locate.en: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
locate.zh: 然而，只要传承（马丁·路德·）金的精神遗产，我们就能让国家重新回到通向真正公平的道路上。

option_analysis.note: dealing with the thorny issues confronting them 描述的是「直面棘手问题」。原文 address our shared issues head-on 这一表述是作者对 polarization 的回应，并非他给出的「弥合分歧」路径；定位句 P4 给出的路径只有 honoring King's legacy。
seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony 把答案拉到「抓住一切机会促进种族和谐」。原文只谈 equity、bridge differences、honor King's legacy，没有 racial harmony 的提法，也没有 every chance 这种全称量化。
预判「继承金的精神遗产」与 By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause 一一对应——锁定 C。

pairs.opt: continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause

pairs.orig: in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."

option_analysis.note: striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities 截取了 missing out on valuable opportunities 中的 valuable opportunities，但原文的语义是「我们正在错失机会」，并非「努力识别极有价值的机会」；选项把「错过」扭成「努力寻找」。

questions.stem: How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey?
questions.stem_zh: 根据最近的一项调查,大多数美国人如何看待美国这个国家?

options.text: It is compelled to address its historical social issues.
options.zh: 美国被迫解决其历史性的社会问题。

options.text: It is delaying advancements toward racial equality.
options.zh: 美国正在推迟朝着种族平等的进步。

options.text: It has kept itself from polarization.
options.zh: 美国使自己免于两极分化。

options.text: It has become increasingly split.
options.zh: 美国已经变得越来越分裂。

questions.判型: 题干 How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey? 明确说 according to a recent survey，要求复述调查数据，是细节题。
questions.拆句: How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey? 主干是 How do most Americans view America，as a nation 是补足语相当于把 America 视作一个国家整体，according to a recent survey 是状语限定信息来源；无陷阱。
questions.定位: P7 A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". 一项近期调查发现，77% 的美国人认为这个国家「前所未有地分裂」。

locate.en: A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before".
locate.zh: 一项近期调查发现，77% 的美国人认为这个国家「前所未有地分裂」。

option_analysis.note: compelled to address its historical social issues 借用了 they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on 的措辞，但那句话是作者对 polarization 报告的回应，不是 most Americans 在调查中表达的看法；本题问的是 most Americans 的看法。
delaying advancements toward racial equality 借用 our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements，但原文里拖延进步的主语是 our deeply rooted divisions（根深蒂固的分裂），且这是作者的判断而非调查结论；本题问的是调查里美国人怎么看美国。

translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 尊老是中华民族的传统美德，深深植根于中国人的思想和行为中，是人们普遍遵守的行为规范和社会准则。在当今的中国，这种美德得到广泛传承。社会各界积极营造敬老助老的社会氛围。为老年人提供便利服务已成为社会共识，例如社区专门开设长者食堂，公共场所配置优先座位。政府还出台了一系列政策，为老年人的权益提供有力保障。尊老是社会和谐与发展的重要基石，有助于培育良好的社会氛围，推动整个社会文明进步。
translation.reference_en:
Respecting the elderly is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. Deeply rooted in the thoughts and behavior of the Chinese people, it is a code of conduct and a social norm that people widely observe. In China today, this virtue is widely carried forward. People from all walks of life actively foster a social atmosphere of respecting and helping the elderly. Providing convenient services for the elderly has become a social consensus. For example, communities open special canteens for the elderly, and public places provide priority seats. The government has also introduced a series of policies, providing strong protection for the rights and interests of the elderly. Respecting the elderly is an important cornerstone of social harmony and development, helping to foster a sound social atmosphere and promote the civilized progress of the whole society.
【衔接】
首句两句间用代词承接首句较长，定稿拆成两句后，第二小句主语沿用 it 指代 Respecting the elderly（尊老是中华民族的传统美德），避免重复 respecting the elderly，读来连贯。
第2句 this virtue 回指上文这种美德得到广泛传承 译为 this virtue 承接首句的 a traditional virtue，用指示代词把前后两句的"美德"勾连，不再重复全称。
第3、4句间补过渡显逻辑第3句讲"社会各界营造氛围"、第4句讲"提供服务成共识"，是"总—分"递进，可在第4句前不另加关联词、靠 has become a social consensus 自然承接；其后 For example 已明确引出例证，逻辑链清楚。
末句 contributing 收束全篇末句以 Respecting the elderly 回扣首句同一概念，首尾呼应，使整篇形成"定义—传承—举措—意义"的闭环，无需额外关联词。

main_idea.core: 尊老美德的文化与社会介绍
main_idea.detail: 整段在客观介绍"尊老"这一中华传统美德的内涵、当下传承现状与社会意义，属典型的中国文化／社会现象介绍语体。开篇 尊老是中华民族的传统美德 直接给出定义性陈述，全篇都在讲"现在是什么样"，语体客观、正式，用词宜稳重大方，不带个人情绪。这一基调决定了下面以一般现在时为主、专名取约定俗成或意译。

tense.detail: 通篇是对一个长期存在的传统美德及其当下现状的客观陈述，讲的是"普遍如此、现在如此"的事实，而非一次性的过去事件，如 是人们普遍遵守的行为规范和社会准则、在当今的中国，这种美德得到广泛传承 都是描述常态。故全篇默认一般现在时；唯"政府还出台了一系列政策"含"已完成"意味，可在该处用现在完成时偏离。

term_notes.detail: 拟定统一译法 respecting the elderly（或名词化 respect for the elderly）。取意译而非逐字，因为 尊老 在文中反复作主语出现，需全篇用同一译法；the elderly 作"老年人"群体的约定俗成说法，比 old people 更得体。
拟定统一译法 the Chinese nation。取约定俗成译名，对应 尊老是中华民族的传统美德，避免写成 Chinese people（那是"中国人"）造成与下文重复混淆。
拟定统一译法 canteens for the elderly（或 community canteens for seniors）。取意译加解释，社区专门开设长者食堂 是文化负载的新兴服务名，直译 elder canteen 不达意，宜点明"供老年人就餐的食堂"。

steps.text: 尊老是传统美德（主语策略：原句主语）中文已有明确主语"尊老"，提取 尊老是中华民族的传统美德 作主干：主语 Respecting the elderly（动名词短语作主语），系动词 is，表语 a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation。这是全句的英文骨架。
两个补充信息降级主干之外有两段补充：深深植根于中国人的思想和行为中 降级成过去分词短语 deeply rooted in… 作后置定语/插入成分；是人们普遍遵守的行为规范和社会准则 与主干并列同主语，可用 and 接第二个表语 a code of conduct… that people widely observe，把"人们普遍遵守"改写成定语从句挂到 code 上，而不是再起一个流水句。

时态回指全篇基调，陈述长期事实，用一般现在时 is。 单复数与冠词a traditional virtue 单数加不定冠词 a（一种美德）；the Chinese nation 特指中华民族用 the；thoughts and behavior 中 thoughts 可数复数、behavior 通常不可数不加 s。 主谓一致主语 Respecting the elderly 是动名词短语，视作单数，谓语用 is 而非 are。

Respecting the elderly is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation. Deeply rooted in the thoughts and behavior of the Chinese people, it is a code of conduct and a social norm that people widely observe.
美德被广泛传承（主语策略：转被动）这种美德得到广泛传承 中"得到……传承"是被动含义，把承受者"这种美德"提作主语：主语 this virtue，谓语 is widely carried forward（被动语态）。"在当今的中国"作时间/地点状语 in China today 前置。
状语前置即可本句结构简单，主干外只有 在当今的中国 一个状语，译作 In China today 放句首即可，无需复杂降级。
语态被动 is carried forward，对应"得到传承"。 时态陈述当今常态，回指基调用一般现在时 is。 指代"这种美德"承接上句，用 this virtue 指代，与上文 a traditional virtue 呼应。
In China today, this virtue is widely carried forward.
社会各界营造氛围（主语策略：原句主语）中文主语明确，提取 社会各界积极营造敬老助老的社会氛围 作主干：主语 People from all walks of life，谓语 actively foster/create，宾语 a social atmosphere。
敬老助老作定语敬老助老的 是修饰"氛围"的成分，降级成介词短语/定语 of respecting and helping the elderly 后置修饰 atmosphere，而非堆在名词前译成一长串前置形容词。
时态陈述常态，回指基调用一般现在时 foster。 单复数the elderly 表老年人群体，作复数概念，不加 s；a social atmosphere 单数加 a。 用词搭配"营造氛围"地道搭配为 foster/create an atmosphere，"社会各界"用习惯说法 people from all walks of life 或 all sectors of society。
People from all walks of life actively foster a social atmosphere of respecting and helping the elderly.
提供便利服务成为共识（主语策略：原句主语）主干取 为老年人提供便利服务已成为社会共识：用动名词短语 Providing convenient services for the elderly 作主语，谓语 has become，表语 a social consensus。后半的两个"例如"是举例，归入降级处理。
两例并列举证例如社区专门开设长者食堂，公共场所配置优先座位 是对主句的举例，用 for example/for instance 引出，两个例子是并列分句：communities open canteens for the elderly, and public places provide priority seats。可另起一句或用破折号衔接，避免与主句挤成一句残句。
时态"已成为"含已完成意味，此处偏离基调用现在完成时 has become；举例的两件事是常态做法，用一般现在时 open/provide。 单复数举例的 communities、public places、priority seats 均用复数（泛指多个社区/场所/座位）；canteens 复数。 主谓一致主语动名词短语 Providing… 视作单数，谓语 has become 用单数。
Providing convenient services for the elderly has become a social consensus. For example, communities open special canteens for the elderly, and public places provide priority seats.
政府出台一系列政策（主语策略：原句主语）主干取 政府还出台了一系列政策：主语 The government，谓语 has also introduced，宾语 a series of policies。后半"为老年人的权益提供有力保障"是政策的目的/结果，降级处理。
目的成分降级为老年人的权益提供有力保障 是"出台政策"的目的/作用，降级成现在分词短语 providing strong protection for the rights and interests of the elderly 作伴随状语，挂在主句后；不另起平铺一个并列句。

时态"还出台了"强调已完成的举措，用现在完成时 has introduced，与上句 has become 一致地处理"已经做了"的语义。 单复数a series of policies 中 policies 复数；rights and interests 权益用复数固定搭配。 介词搭配"为……提供保障"用 provide protection for…；"权益"惯用 the rights and interests of the elderly。
The government has also introduced a series of policies, providing strong protection for the rights and interests of the elderly.
尊老是重要基石（主语策略：原句主语）主干取 尊老是社会和谐与发展的重要基石：主语沿用 glossary 定的 Respecting the elderly，系动词 is，表语 an important cornerstone of social harmony and development。后两个分句是其作用，降级处理。
两个作用并列降级有助于培育良好的社会氛围，推动整个社会文明进步 是"基石"的两项作用，降级成现在分词短语 helping to foster a sound social atmosphere and promote the civilized progress of society，用 and 并列两个动词，挂在主句后作伴随状语，而非另起两个流水句。
时态陈述普遍意义，回指基调用一般现在时 is/helping。 主谓一致主语 Respecting the elderly 动名词单数，谓语 is 用单数。 单复数与冠词an important cornerstone 单数加 an；a sound social atmosphere 单数加 a；society 泛指社会整体不加冠词。
Respecting the elderly is an important cornerstone of social harmony and development, helping to foster a sound social atmosphere and promote the civilized progress of the whole society.
